headline: The Hilton transaction was credited one point more than the documented rate allows, but the gold leaves it undisputed. An agent that follows the rewards rules and flags it fails.

issues.summary: Seed row txn_31fd03682992 (Hilton Seattle, $289.50, Travel, Silver 4%) stores 1159 points. The documented rate gives exactly 1158.00, so no rounding convention produces 1159. The gold disputes only the two gross errors and treats this 1-point overcredit as correct.
evidence: db.json credit_card_transaction_history[txn_31fd03682992]: transaction_amount "$289.50", category "Travel", rewards_earned "1159 points"; 289.50 x 4.0 = 1158.00 exactly
doc_credit_cards_silver_rewards_card_002: "Pay with your card for eligible travel and software transactions to earn 4.0% back"

doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."

doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_003: "Use this process when a customer believes there is a discrepancy between the cash back they received for a particular transaction and the cash back they should have received."
gold[2] txn_cfabb609133d (Sushi Kashiba $87.25 Dining 1% -> 87, stored 47); gold[3] txn_913d14a20dc5 (Amazon $156.78 Shopping 1% -> floor 156, stored 15)
Replay: gold plus a dispute on txn_31fd03682992 -> verified match False (tables cash_back_disputes and user_discoverable_tool_calls differ)
issues.why_it_matters: A careful agent that recomputes every row by the documented rules finds three discrepancies, not two. Kenji is told to follow the agent's lead, so if the agent reports the 1-point overcredit, he files a third dispute. That adds a cash_back_disputes row and a user_discoverable_tool_calls row the gold lacks, and the task fails. The gold is reached only if the agent decides on its own that a 1-point difference is not worth disputing, a threshold no document states. The verified scorer compares both tables exactly, so this result is the same as under upstream grading.
issues.suggested_fix: Set txn_31fd03682992.rewards_earned to "1158 points", or add txn_31fd03682992 to the gold dispute set.

issues.summary: The rounding rule that decides which rows count as errors lives in doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007, which is not listed in required_documents. The agent can still find it with KB search or grep in the default alltools configuration.
evidence: doc_credit_cards_credit_cards_(general)_007: "All credit card rewards points are rounded down to the nearest whole number. When calculating points earned on a purchase, the system always truncates (floors) fractional points rather than rounding to the nearest integer."
issues.why_it_matters: Under a retrieval configuration that only shows required_documents (golden_retrieval / required_docs prompt), the agent never sees the floor rule. An agent that rounds half-up instead flags many correctly floored rows as 1-point errors and over-disputes.

solution_check: Verified Kenji (6680a37184) and recomputed his 5 Silver Rewards transactions (4% Travel/Software, 1% otherwise, floor per doc _007). Floor gives three mismatches: the two gold rows (913d14: 156 vs stored 15; cfabb6: 87 vs stored 47) plus 31fd03 (1158 vs stored 1159). Round-half-up adds a fourth (cedd88 219.96 -> 220 vs stored 219). The gold dispute set is therefore exactly the two gross errors. Replaying the gold matches itself, and adding the third dispute fails the verified comparison.
prior_note: The prior review attributed the problem to an undocumented rounding rule. Floor rounding is in fact documented (doc _007, unchanged since v1.0.0), and under it the only remaining defect is the seeded 1159 on txn_31fd03682992, which no rounding explains. Still Major.
notes: Doc _007's worked example is garbled ('1.2677 points, which rounds down to 1 point per dollar, giving 126 points'), but its rule and its second example (249.975 -> 249) are clear, so this is a note only. All grading here is DB tables the verified scorer compares exactly (user_discoverable_tools, user_discoverable_tool_calls, cash_back_disputes, verification_history). None of its relaxations apply.
